newsitem.title: JAPAN: Strong quake hits Tokyo, no damage or casualties.
newsitem.headline: Strong quake hits Tokyo, no damage or casualties.

text.p: A strong earthquake shook Tokyo and surrounding areas on Wednesday morning, Japan's Meteorological Agency said.
The Tokyo Fire Agency said there were no immediate reports of any damage or casualties from the quake, which measured 6.6 on the Richter scale.
The tremor struck the Tokyo area at 11.37 a.m. (0237 GMT).
Japanese television said the tremor was strongest in northern Chiba Prefecture, adjoining the capital.
Officials at Tokyo's main international airport at Narita, northern Chiba, said the airport had closed its runways for about 10 minutes after the quake but then resumed operations.
Trains in the area, which are programmed to halt automatically in case of a major earthquake, were reported to be running as normal despite the tremor.
The epicentre, the point on the surface above an earthquake's focus, was in the Pacific Ocean 150 km (90 miles) east of Tokyo, the Meteorological Agency said.
The agency said there was a tsunami (tidal wave) warning in effect for Japan's Pacific Ocean coast around Tokyo.
Television reports said the quake measured four on the Japanese scale of seven in northern Chiba. It measured three on the same scale in Tokyo itself.
The Japanese scale measures ground motion in a given area in relation to the epicentre, while the Richter scale measures the absolute seismic energy of an earthquake at its epicentre.
